reproducibility.note: all second-pass experiments are offline replays of recorded data and are deterministic

independent_test.headline: The first audit reported that no independent test split existed. A complete, episode-disjoint 189-episode collection does exist (data/raw_v2_stale_projection). Headline metrics are re-evaluated on it here with every threshold and checkpoint held fixed.

provenance_and_validity.conclusion: occ_grid differs ~3x between collections while per-object tier distribution and mean visibility agree to within 0.020 / 0.006. Consistent with the documented BevProjector defect being confined to the BEV grid. The per-object pipeline is therefore treated as sound for this test set; the occlusion detector is NOT evaluated on it.
provenance_and_validity.occlusion_detector_on_this_set: REFUSED -- ground truth grid is the corrupted one

not_evaluated_here.occlusion_detector: REFUSED. This collection's occ_grid is the pre-fix, sign-error ground truth. Scoring the detector against it would be scoring against known-wrong labels.

caveats: This collection was archived, not discarded, precisely because its BEV grid was wrong. Its use here rests on the defect being confined to that grid, which is documented and re-verified empirically above -- but it is an inference, not a guarantee.
No hyperparameter, threshold or checkpoint was selected using this set.
The classifier's crops come from labels/, which excludes fully-occluded actors in this collection exactly as in the training one.

intent_lead_time.ground_truth: time_to_entry_s from intent_labels.npz (project's own corridor definition)
intent_lead_time.evaluation_design: per band: positives = observations whose true time-to-entry falls in the band; negatives = the common pool of all will_cross==False observations scored by that configuration. Recall is band-specific; precision and AUC share the common negative pool and are comparable across bands for a given configuration.

interpretation.headline: Fusion substantially extends the detection horizon. At 1.0-1.5s before corridor entry fused recall is 0.696 vs camera 0.306 (2.3x); at 1.5-2.0s it is 0.545 vs 0.036. Radar alone detects essentially nothing at any lead time, consistent with its structural lateral blindness.
interpretation.read_recall_not_precision: Precision and F1 are NOT comparable across bands and must not be quoted per band. Every band shares one large negative pool (thousands of non-crossing observations) while the positive count falls from ~1600 in the nearest band to a handful in the far bands, so precision is driven to near zero by construction regardless of model quality. Recall (band-specific by definition) and ROC-AUC are the interpretable columns.
interpretation.label_horizon_vs_realised: Labels use a 3.0s horizon but realised entry times cluster hard at the near end: of 6,663 observations with a ground-truth entry time, the 0.0-0.5s band holds ~1,600 of the positives each configuration scores, while bands beyond 1.5s hold fewer than 20. The dataset therefore supports lead-time claims only out to about 1.5s.
interpretation.radar_auc_artifact: Radar ROC-AUC appears to RISE with lead time (0.734 to 0.970) while its recall stays at 0.000. AUC is rank-based and does not require the model to cross the decision threshold; with n as low as 1-14 positives those values are unstable and must not be reported as radar improving at long range.

hidden_target_diagnosis.question: is the 15-event limit data, or an evaluation restriction?

attrition.stage_1_to_2_cause: The actor was never CONFIRMED-tracked while visible, so there is no state to seed a hidden-target predictor from. MultiObjectTracker requires MIN_HITS_TO_CONFIRM=3 consecutive associations. This is a genuine property of the pipeline, not an evaluation artefact: with no prior track there is literally nothing to propagate.
attrition.stage_2_to_3_cause: re-emerged (or amodal truth ended) before the shortest 0.5s horizon could be scored

verdict.classification: A + pipeline-inherent: genuinely few scorable events
verdict.explanation: Of 202 ground-truth occlusion transitions, only 32 (15.8%) involved an actor the tracker had already confirmed, and only 15 of those stayed hidden long enough to score. The dominant loss is upstream of the hidden-target evaluation: most actors that go behind an occluder were never solidly tracked in the first place. That is a real limitation of the perception chain, not a bug in the evaluation, and it cannot be fixed by changing the scoring.

actions_considered_and_rejected: Lowering MIN_HITS_TO_CONFIRM to admit more events -- rejected: it would change the tracker's behaviour, i.e. the system under test.
Widening the 5 m association gate -- rejected: same reason, and it would flatter the result by admitting looser matches.
Seeding the hidden predictor from ground truth instead of the last confirmed estimate -- rejected: that leaks privileged state and is not what pipeline._handoff does at runtime.

fault_severity.question: How much do the three SILENT failures degrade the pipeline as severity rises, and does the health monitor ever notice?
fault_severity.method: each fault is the shipped function from scripts.adversarial_test, invoked via functools.partial with a different value of its own existing severity keyword; no new fault model was written
fault_severity.denominator_note: metrics are aggregated over all VRU observations in the sampled episodes; n_detections is reported per condition

interpretation.headline_monitor_never_wakes: Across every severity tested -- up to 8x the shipped magnitude (radar_bias 20 m, radar_clutter 320 spurious returns, extrinsic_drift 32 deg) -- radar health never fell below the 0.6 degraded threshold. It stayed in 0.83-0.99. The first audit showed these faults are undetected at one severity; this shows they are undetected across the whole range, so it is not a threshold-tuning problem.

damage_is_real_and_dose_dependent.radar_bias: v_lat MAE 0.893 -> 2.676 m/s and intent AUC 0.871 -> 0.707 as offset goes 0.5 -> 20 m
damage_is_real_and_dose_dependent.radar_clutter: v_lat MAE 1.026 -> 1.799 m/s and position RMSE +1.148 m at n_extra=320
damage_is_real_and_dose_dependent.extrinsic_drift: position RMSE +0.605 m at 32 deg; intent AUC stays high (0.90-0.93)

interpretation.PERVERSE_radar_clutter_raises_health: The most important finding here. Radar health INCREASES monotonically with clutter: [(10, 0.9125329644444751), (20, 0.9417914880952382), (40, 0.9666865851866483), (80, 0.9784146724888007), (160, 0.9827911655757112), (320, 0.9933333333333333)]. perception.radar_confidence is documented as a density + cluster-tightness proxy because CARLA exposes no SNR, so injecting spurious returns raises measured density and the sensor scores as HEALTHIER precisely as it becomes less trustworthy. This is a structural defect in the health metric, not a tuning issue, and no threshold on this statistic can fix it.
interpretation.non_monotonic_caveat: Some cells are non-monotonic (radar_bias position RMSE peaks at 5 m then falls; small biases marginally improve position). With 24 episodes these wiggles are within noise and only the overall trend should be quoted.

distributions.denominator: paired observation = (episode, frame, actor) tracked by all three modes AND moving laterally >= 0.3 m/s
distributions.why_tails_matter: A mean hides whether a configuration is consistently adequate or occasionally catastrophic. For a braking decision the 95th percentile error is the operative number, not the average.

effect_sizes.note: complements the first pass's bootstrap p-values: a p-value reports whether a difference is distinguishable from zero, an effect size reports whether it is large enough to care about

spearman_uncertainty_vs_error.interpretation: positive rho means higher uncertainty accompanies more errors, i.e. the uncertainty is ordered with difficulty

classifier_size_analysis.reason: raw_predictions_val.npz stores tier and visibility but not the crop's pixel dimensions, and re-deriving them would require re-running inference. Visibility fraction is reported instead, which is the difficulty axis the project itself defines.

spatial_errors.question: where in the BEV grid does the occlusion detector fail?
spatial_errors.method: same fixed operating point and same held-out frame set as AUDIT-B-OCCLUSION-HOLDOUT (seed 1234, sweep's seed-0 sample excluded); nothing was retuned
spatial_errors.denominator: BEV grid CELLS; each frame contributes 400

boundary_vs_interior.definition: interior = GT-OCCLUDED cell whose four 4-neighbours are all GT-OCCLUDED; boundary = every other GT-OCCLUDED cell

leakage_audit.question: does episode-disjoint splitting leave any near-identical crop on both sides of the train/val boundary?
leakage_audit.method: 64-bit dHash of every crop at its recorded box; exact hash collisions and Hamming<=3 near-duplicates (found exactly via 4-band LSH) counted between the two sides

context_within_episode_consecutive_simil.note: NOT a valid comparator and must not be quoted as one: this walks hashes in sorted VALUE order, not frame order, so it does not measure consecutive-frame similarity. Retained only to record what was computed.
